title: Mouthpiece from Barney Bigard and study with him
summary: Bigard gave him a mouthpiece in 1933 and taught him while Tio was away in New York.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: And what about the mouthpiece? Did you do anything to the mouthpiece or did you just have the same mouthpiece?

Well, the mouthpiece that I'm using now is a mouthpiece that was given to me by Bonnie Begaard. Oh, yeah. Yes, Begaard gave me that mouthpiece back in 33, but before then it was the same regular stout

mouthpiece from the horn that I had used. And do you find any difference in the tone between the two mouthpieces? Well, yes, I did. That's why I began using it. It made it a little broader because it was more of an open layer. But about the same kind of reed you've always used? Just a little softer reed. That's a soft. Now than what I had been using before.

I was using a much harder reed because the mouthpiece was a little closer. But the mouthpiece that was given to me by Begaard, by the layer being a little open, it made I use a softer reed. You know Begaard, when my father and I had gone to New York, well he taught me also. Oh yeah? Yeah. Because after they had gone and Lorenzo said he didn't want me to just be idling around and taking things on myself. So he had the choice of either sending me to Adolf Alexander or Begaard. So he said, well I think I'd rather send you to Begaard. Now at the time that he sent me to Begaard, Begaard wasn't playing clarinet at all. He had stopped playing clarinet. In other words, around here they wouldn't even employ him as a clarinet. They thought that he had played so bad. But Lorenzo said he thought that he would be the better instructor for me. He would be the better instructor for me. And I stayed with him until they came back. And Begaard didn't pick up these clarinet, he told me until around 1925 or 1926 somewhere when with the Olives and Van Olives. We were in Chicago. I thought that he really worked on it. What's the matter? You got that thing up there for you? Why don't you try and clear the thing? And he said it looked like they gave him an admission. And then he began studying hard on it again.
